name: mpt_wait_db_ack
prose: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the interrupt status register with mpt_rd_intr; if the doorbell is not busy (MPT_DB_IS_BUSY false) it records i in the global maxwait_ack if i is larger than the stored value and returns MPT_OK immediately, with no delay after that successful read; otherwise it calls DELAY(200) and polls again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT polls it returns MPT_FAIL.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: no delay follows the successful poll (mpt.c:912-915); the delay of 200 us is after each unsuccessful one. Original reviewer's omission points are covered by the explicit MPT_OK/MPT_FAIL returns and the busy-wait. Function at 906-919. Read in full.

name: mpt_wait_db_int
prose: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the interrupt status register with mpt_rd_intr; if a doorbell interrupt is asserted (MPT_DB_INTR true) it records i in the global maxwait_int if larger and returns MPT_OK immediately without a delay; otherwise it calls DELAY(100) and polls again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT polls it returns MPT_FAIL.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: no delay follows the successful poll (mpt.c:928-931). Function at 922-935. Read in full.

name: mpt_wait_state
prose: Precondition: mpt is a valid mpt_softc. It loops i from 0 to MPT_MAX_WAIT - 1: it reads the doorbell register with mpt_rd_db; if MPT_STATE of the value equals state it records i in the global maxwait_state if larger and returns MPT_OK immediately without a delay; otherwise it calls DELAY(100) and reads again. After MPT_MAX_WAIT reads it returns MPT_FAIL.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: no delay follows the successful read (mpt.c:957-960). Function at 950-964. Read in full.

name: mpt_fc_els_reply_handler
prose: Precondition: mpt is an initialised adapter, req the request the reply belongs to, reply_frame the reply message. The function returns TRUE on every path that was read. If the IOC status is not success it logs, sets mpt->disabled to 1 when the status is MPI_IOCSTATUS_INVALID_STATE, and returns TRUE. For a MPI_FUNCTION_FC_LINK_SRVC_RSP reply it finds req in mpt->els_cmd_ptrs (a KASSERT, effective only with INVARIANTS, requires it to be there), removes it from mpt->request_pending_list, marks it done instead of queued and reposts it with mpt_fc_post_els. For a MPI_FUNCTION_FC_PRIMITIVE_SEND reply it removes req from the pending list, marks it done, and frees it if it timed out or nobody is waiting for it (otherwise it is left for the waiter); then returns. Any function other than LINK_SRVC_BUF_POST logs and returns. For a buffer-post reply with MsgLength <= 5 it logs and returns, as it does when MPI_LS_BUF_POST_REPLY_FLAG_NO_RSP_NEEDED is set. Otherwise it takes the request at mpt->els_cmd_ptrs[TransactionContext] and decodes R_CTL, type and command: for an ELS PRLI it builds an accept payload in the ELS buffer (target/initiator role bits set from mpt->role), removes the request from the pending list, marks it done and sends the response with mpt_fc_els_send_response (20 bytes), without reposting; PRLO is handled the same with a different payload; other ELS commands only log and are reposted. For an ABTS frame it logs, and if the RX_ID is in range, mpt->tgt_cmd_ptrs is non-NULL, the target command has a back pointer, and its context id and initiator tag match RX_ID and OX_ID, it logs the target state and calls mpt_abort_target_cmd (logging if that cannot be started); in every ABTS case (including the mismatch cases that skip the abort) it rewrites the frame's R_CTL to BA_ACC and sends a 12-byte response through mpt_fc_els_send_response. Any other R_CTL/type is logged. Unless a response was sent, the request is removed from the pending list, marked done and reposted with mpt_fc_post_els.
note: Packet name for this item was truncated; the function is mpt_fc_els_reply_handler at mpt_cam.c:2756-2989 (slice 2850-3150 started inside it). The old prose said 'ABTS ... skip the target abort but still send a BA_ACC', which agrees with this code (2926-2977). Not read line by line: the debug logging lines and the elsbuf contents. The part of the slice after 2989 is another function.

name: mpt_scsi_tgt_reply_handler
prose: Precondition: mpt is a valid softc, req a valid request and reply_frame either NULL (a context/turbo reply) or a valid reply message. If reply_frame is NULL it switches on the target state of req: TGT_STATE_LOADED calls mpt_scsi_tgt_atio; MOVING_DATA with no associated request panics, with no associated CCB and is_local zero panics, with no CCB and is_local set it frees the associated request and sends status with mpt_scsi_tgt_status and returns; with a CCB it clears the timeout, counts the transfer, frees the associated request and, if the CCB has no CAM_SEND_STATUS flag, completes the CCB with CAM_REQ_CMP and sets state TGT_STATE_IN_CAM (releasing the SIM queue if outofbeer), else sends the status; SENDING_STATUS and MOVING_DATA_AND_STATUS (panic if there is no associated request) complete the CCB if there is one (CAM_REQ_CMP, CAM_SENT_SENSE if sense was sent), free the associated request, repost the target command buffer with mpt_post_target_command and call xpt_done on the CCB; TGT_STATE_NIL sets TGT_STATE_LOADED; other states only log. It returns TRUE. If reply_frame is non-NULL it logs and switches on the function: for MPI_FUNCTION_TARGET_CMD_BUFFER_POST a non-success status leaves req unchanged, a success asserts (INVARIANTS only) that the state is TGT_STATE_LOADING, assigns a serial number and sets state TGT_STATE_LOADED; for TARGET_ASSIST and TARGET_STATUS_SEND it logs, removes req from the pending list and frees it; for TARGET_MODE_ABORT it logs the abort completion, removes req from the list and frees it; other functions are only logged. It returns TRUE.
note: Packet name unnamed target-mode reply handler is mpt_scsi_tgt_reply_handler at mpt_cam.c:5094-5342 (read in full). The old prose covered only the reply_frame-non-NULL part (the slice start 5273); the turbo reply_frame == NULL part at 5102-5271 is now described. The panic calls at 5126, 5132 and 5198 are reached only on inconsistent state.

name: mpt_scsi_tgt_atio
prose: Precondition: req is a target request whose mpt_tgt_state is TGT_STATE_LOADED (otherwise the function dumps the state and panics), reply_desc is a valid reply descriptor, and req->req_vbuf offset by MPT_RQSL(mpt) holds the FC, SAS or SPI target command buffer. It zeroes the target state, sets it to TGT_STATE_IN_CAM and records reply_desc and the tag id. Then by transport: for FC, a nonzero task-management byte selects a task management function (query task set, abort task set, clear task set, query async event, LUN reset, target reset or clear ACA); an unrecognised value sends SCSI_STATUS_OK with mpt_scsi_tgt_status and returns before tgt->itag and tgt->resid are set; otherwise the tag action is derived from the control byte, and tgt->resid (data length), the CDB, LUN and tgt->itag (OX_ID) are taken from the FCP buffer; for SAS and SPI the CDB, LUN and tgt->itag are taken from their buffers and tgt->resid is left at zero. It then picks a LUN resource: if the LUN is out of range, target mode is disabled or the LUN is not enabled, the wildcard resource is used when mpt->twildcard is set, else (when no task management function is pending) it answers locally: INQUIRY (with EVPD clear) and REQUEST SENSE are answered with mpt_scsi_tgt_local and return; REPORT_LUNS returns without sending any status; every other command, and INQUIRY with EVPD set, gets SCSI_STATUS_CHECK_COND with sense data built in the function; if a task management function is pending and no resource is available the function answers SCSI_STATUS_OK. A task management function with a resource is passed to mpt_scsi_tgt_tsk_mgmt. Otherwise it takes the first ATIO queued on the LUN resource; if none is queued it sends SCSI_STATUS_QUEUE_FULL (or SCSI_STATUS_BUSY when target mode is disabled); else it removes the ATIO, fills in LUN, tag id, initiator id, the 16-byte CDB and the tag action and completes it with xpt_done. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the invalid FC task-management path returns at mpt_cam.c:4898-4903 before tgt->itag and tgt->resid are set. Original reviewer right that resid is set only in the FC branch (4924). Real function at 4814-5072 (slice 4724-5016). Read in full; helper functions not read; the sense bytes built for unmanaged LUNs were not examined.

name: mrsas_aen_handler
prose: Precondition: sc may be NULL. If sc is NULL it prints "invalid instance!" and returns; if remove_in_progress or reset_in_progress is set it prints a message and returns; if sc->evt_detail_mem is NULL it prints "invalid evt_detail" and returns (so these returns are not free of side effects: each prints a message). Otherwise it acts on the event code in evt_detail_mem: MR_EVT_PD_INSERTED and MR_EVT_PD_REMOVED call mrsas_get_pd_list and scan sim_1 if it succeeds (a failure jumps to the end without registering a new AEN); MR_EVT_LD_OFFLINE, MR_EVT_CFG_CLEARED and MR_EVT_LD_DELETED scan sim_0; MR_EVT_LD_CREATED calls mrsas_get_ld_list and scans sim_0 (failure skips AEN registration); MR_EVT_CTRL_HOST_BUS_SCAN_REQUESTED, MR_EVT_FOREIGN_CFG_IMPORTED and MR_EVT_LD_STATE_CHANGE set a flag that makes it call get_pd_list then scan sim_1 and get_ld_list then scan sim_0 (any failure skips registration); MR_EVT_CTRL_PROP_CHANGED calls mrsas_get_ctrl_info (failure skips registration); any other code does nothing. If none of those failed it computes seq_num = the event's seq_num + 1, returns if sc->aen_cmd is non-NULL, and otherwise registers a new AEN for locale ALL and class DEBUG with mrsas_register_aen under sc->aen_lock, printing an error if registration returns nonzero. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the NULL sc and NULL evt_detail_mem returns print messages (mrsas.c:4926-4929, 4976-4978). Original reviewer right that CTRL_PROP_CHANGED does no scan and that the default code does nothing. Real function at 4918-5016 (slice 4912-5072). Read in full; the list/scan/register helpers not read.

name: msk_watchdog
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the interface lock (MSK_IF_LOCK_ASSERT). If msk_watchdog_timer is 0 it returns with nothing changed. Otherwise it decrements the timer, and if the decremented value is still nonzero it returns (the timer has been decremented but nothing else changed). When the timer reaches 0: if MSK_FLAG_LINK is not set it counts one IFCOUNTER_OERRORS, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING and calls msk_init_locked, then returns without calling msk_start_locked; if the link flag is set it prints a watchdog message, counts one output error, clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls msk_init_locked and then calls msk_start_locked if the send queue is not empty. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the timer is decremented on the path where it stays nonzero (if_msk.c:2938), so 'changed nothing' was wrong for that case. Original reviewer right that the missed-link path does not call msk_start_locked (2941-2948). Real function at 2931-2957 (slice 2819-3106). Read in full.

name: mthca_alloc_srq
prose: Precondition: dev, pd, attr and srq are valid; attr->max_wr and attr->max_sge are the requested sizes; udata is non-NULL for a userspace SRQ and NULL for a kernel SRQ. It returns -EINVAL if attr->max_wr or attr->max_sge exceeds the device limits, or, on a non-mem-free device, if the descriptor size exceeds dev->limits.max_desc_sz. It sets the SRQ size (one more than requested; rounded up to a power of two on mem-free devices) and allocates an SRQ number with mthca_alloc, returning -ENOMEM if none is available. On mem-free devices it takes the ICM table entry (mthca_table_get; error returned) and, for a kernel SRQ, allocates a doorbell (-ENOMEM if that fails). It then allocates a mailbox (PTR_ERR on failure) and the SRQ buffer with mthca_alloc_srq_buf, initialises the lock, refcount (1), waitqueue and mutex, builds the SRQ context and calls mthca_SW2HW_SRQ; a nonzero result unwinds and is returned. It then inserts the SRQ in the SRQ table under the table lock; if mthca_array_set fails it calls mthca_HW2SW_SRQ and then unwinds, and the value returned is that of mthca_HW2SW_SRQ (a HW2SW failure is only logged), which can be 0 even though creation failed. On success it frees the mailbox, sets first_free to 0 and last_free to max - 1, writes the actual max_wr (max - 1) and max_sge back into attr and returns 0. The unwinding releases, in reverse order, the SRQ buffer (kernel SRQs), the mailbox, the doorbell (kernel SRQ on mem-free devices), the ICM table reference (the mthca_table_put call is not conditioned on mem-free in the code) and the SRQ number.
note: Packet name mthca_create_srq is not in mthca_srq.c; the real function is mthca_alloc_srq at mthca_srq.c:200-319 (read in full). Round 17 reviewer is right: if mthca_HW2SW_SRQ fails the SRQ may remain in hardware, which is only logged (297-299). The old claim that on mthca_array_set failure the function returns the HW2SW status (possibly 0) is kept (296-318).

name: mvs_reset
prose: Precondition: dev is an mvs channel device with consistent softc and slot arrays; the global dumping flag may be set. It freezes the SIM queue once, and if a reset countdown is active (ch->resetting nonzero) it clears it, stops the reset callout and releases one queue freeze. It requeues frozen CCBs, turns EDMA off, writes 0 to DMA_C and ends every slot at or above MVS_SLOT_RUNNING with mvs_end_transaction(..., MVS_ERR_INNOCENT). It completes every held CCB with xpt_done and decrements numhslots, releases the SIM queue if ch->toslots is nonzero, clears eslots, toslots, fatalerr and fake_busy, announces AC_BUS_RESET and resets the controller (EDMA interrupt mask written 0, ATA reset pulse, mvs_errata) and the SATA PHY. If the PHY reset finds no device it sets ch->devices to 0, clears the SATA error register, clears the EDMA interrupt cause, writes the EDMA interrupt mask register as ~EDMA_IE_TRANSIENT (so all non-transient EDMA interrupts are unmasked, not masked off), releases the SIM queue and returns. Otherwise it waits for BSY and DRQ to clear (31000 ms when dumping, else without a wait); if the wait fails, in dump mode it only prints a message and in normal mode it sets ch->resetting to 310. It then sets ch->devices to 1, clears the SATA error and EDMA interrupt cause registers, writes the interrupt mask as ~EDMA_IE_TRANSIENT, and if ch->resetting is set starts the reset callout (hz / 10, mvs_reset_to) instead of releasing the SIM queue, otherwise releases the SIM queue; so in dump mode the queue is released even if the device was not ready.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the interrupt mask is written as ~EDMA_IE_TRANSIENT (mvs.c:2080, 2099), not zero, so interrupts are not simply masked. Original reviewer right that the dump-time wait failure still releases the queue (2087-2103). Real function at 2026-2104 (slice 1935-2195). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: mwl_watchdog
prose: Precondition: arg is a valid mwl_softc and this is the watchdog callout. It first re-arms the callout to run again after hz ticks on every call. If sc_tx_timer is 0 it returns; otherwise it decrements the timer and returns if the new value is still above 0. When the timer reaches 0 and sc_running is set and sc_invalid is clear, it calls mwl_hal_setkeepalive: if that returns nonzero it prints "transmit timeout (firmware hung?)", otherwise it prints "transmit timeout"; it then increments ic_oerrors by one and mst_watchdog. If sc_running is clear or sc_invalid is set, nothing is printed and no counter is changed.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the 'firmware hung' message is printed when mwl_hal_setkeepalive returns nonzero (if_mwl.c:4563-4565), not when it succeeds. Original reviewer right about the sc_invalid guard (4562). Real function at 4553-4576 (slice 4380-4639). Read in full.

name: mvs_legacy_intr
prose: Precondition: dev is an mvs channel device handling a legacy (non-EDMA) PIO or ATAPI interrupt; slot 0 is the PIO slot. The function returns nothing. It reads the status; if slot 0 is below MVS_SLOT_RUNNING it returns without doing anything else. If the status is BUSY it returns at once when poll is nonzero, otherwise it re-reads the status after DELAY(100) and again after DELAY(1000) and returns if still BUSY. If the error bit is set it ends the transaction with MVS_ERR_TFE. For an ATA PIO command it stores the status, and for a data command reads (data-in, waiting for DRQ for up to 1000 ms; a timeout prints, freezes the SIM queue, sets the slot's bit in ch->toslots and ends with MVS_ERR_TIMEOUT) and advances donecount; if more data remains it, for a write, waits for DRQ (same timeout handling), writes the next chunk and returns, and for a read returns to wait for the next interrupt; if no more data remains, or for no-data commands, it ends the transaction with MVS_ERR_NONE. For an ATAPI command with basic DMA it sets MVS_ERR_TFE if the device-write-fault bit or the DMA error bit is set, clears DMA_C and ends the transaction. For an ATAPI PIO command it decodes the interrupt reason and status: the command-out phase prints and returns without ending the transaction; the write and read data phases transfer the data, update donecount and transfersize and return (a write phase on a data-in command, or a read phase on a data-out command, ends with MVS_ERR_TFE); DONEDRQ prints a warning, moves one chunk if the direction is in or out (MVS_ERR_TFE otherwise) and then falls through to the end handling of the done phase; the abort and done phases end with MVS_ERR_TFE if the error or write-fault bit is set, else MVS_ERR_NONE; an unknown phase ends with MVS_ERR_TFE. The transaction is ended with mvs_end_transaction(slot, et).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the ATAPI CMDOUT phase (mvs.c:925-928) and the final ATA PIO write chunk (900-903) return without ending the transaction. Original reviewer right that the 'slot is running' precondition is replaced by an early return (848-849). Real function at 835-1011 (slice 820-1081). Read in full.

name: mxge_attach
prose: Precondition: dev is a device bound to this driver with a zeroed softc; the function creates its own taskqueue, parent DMA tag, ifnet, mutexes and callout. It fetches tunables, creates the taskqueue and a parent DMA tag (error from bus_dma_tag_create goes to abort_with_tq, which only drains and frees the taskqueue and returns the error). It then allocates the ifnet, initialises the command and driver mutexes, sets up PCI config space and maps the memory BAR (ENXIO if it cannot be mapped, via abort_with_lock, or if the computed SRAM size exceeds the mapped size, via abort_with_mem_res). It reads and parses the EEPROM strings (mxge_parse_strings error returned), enables write combining and allocates DMA memory for the command buffer, zero-pad and dmabench areas (each failing allocation unwinds the earlier ones and returns its error), selects the firmware (mxge_select_firmware), probes slices, allocates slices (mxge_alloc_slices), resets the NIC (mxge_reset), allocates rings (mxge_alloc_rings) and adds the interrupt (mxge_add_irq); each failure unwinds in reverse through the abort labels (rings, slices, dmabench, zeropad and cmd DMA, memory resource and bus mastering, mutexes, ifnet free, parent DMA tag, taskqueue) and returns the error. On success it sets the ifnet capabilities and handlers, initialises and probes the media, calls ether_ifattach, changes the MTU if mxge_initial_mtu differs from ETHERMTU (the result of mxge_change_mtu is ignored), adds sysctls, sets the transmit and flush functions, starts the taskqueue thread (the return value of taskqueue_start_threads is not checked), arms the tick callout and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: taskqueue_start_threads (if_mxge.c:4790) is called without checking its return, so returning 0 does not guarantee the taskqueue thread started. Real function at 4609-4820 (slice 4654-4875 cut the head). Mostly read: the control flow, error labels and the main calls were read; the capability and handler setup lines 4732-4775 were only skimmed, and the details of the abort_with_mem_res and abort_with_lock cleanup (lines 4805-4815) were not read line by line.

name: netmap_ioctl
prose: Precondition: priv is the netmap_priv_d of the calling file, data points to the argument for cmd (a struct nmreq_header for NIOCCTRL, otherwise the legacy argument). The function returns an errno-style value (0 on success). NIOCCTRL: it returns EINVAL for an out-of-range API version (before copying anything), copies the request in with nmreq_copyin (returning that error), and dispatches on the request type, each case storing the callee's result in error: REGISTER (takes NMG_LOCK; EBUSY if the file is already registered; resolves the port with netmap_get_na, using a memory allocator when an id is given and EINVAL for an unknown memory id; EBUSY if the port is kernel-owned; EIO for a virtio-net header mismatch; calls netmap_do_regif, validates a CSB option with netmap_csb_validate, reads memory info with netmap_mem_get_info and checks the options with nmreq_checkoptions; releases NMG_LOCK), PORT_INFO_GET, VALE_ATTACH and DETACH (netmap_bdg_attach and netmap_bdg_detach), PORT_HDR_SET and GET (ENXIO if the port cannot be found, EINVAL for a bad header length), VALE_LIST, VALE_NEWIF and DELIF (nm_vi_create and nm_vi_destroy), VALE_POLLING_ENABLE and DISABLE (nm_bdg_polling), POOLS_INFO_GET (netmap_mem_finalize and netmap_mem_pools_info_get), CSB_ENABLE (EINVAL if the file is already in a state that does not allow it, else netmap_csb_validate), SYNC_KLOOP_START and STOP (netmap_sync_kloop and netmap_sync_kloop_stop); an unknown request type gives EINVAL. At the end of NIOCCTRL it writes the reply header back with nmreq_copyout(hdr, error) and returns the resulting error (the copyout can add an EFAULT). NIOCTXSYNC and NIOCRXSYNC: ENXIO if the port is not registered, EBUSY if the CSB mode is active, and for each ring tried, a failed nm_kr_tryget is converted to EIO if it reported an error and to 0 (success, the ring is skipped) if it did not. Any other cmd is handed to netmap_ioctl_legacy and its result returned.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: at netmap.c:3189-3190 a failed nm_kr_tryget gives error = (error ? EIO : 0), so the old claim of EIO for a failed ring tryget was incomplete. The packet name netmap_ioctl is correct; the real function is at 2739-3238 (slice 3110-3364 started inside it). Partly read: only the return, error assignment, case and lock lines of the whole function (500 lines) and not the bodies; whether references (na, ifp, nmd) are released on every path was not verified and is not claimed. The old statement that every path drops all references and releases NMG_LOCK is therefore removed.

name: netmap_bwrap_bdg_ctl
prose: Precondition: hdr and na are valid and na is a bridge-wrapper adapter. For hdr->nr_reqtype == NETMAP_REQ_VALE_ATTACH: it returns EINVAL if the request's registration ring id is nonzero or its mode is neither NR_REG_ALL_NIC nor NR_REG_NIC_SW; returns EBUSY if NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY(na) is true; returns 0 without any change if bna->na_kpriv is already set (the code checks this after the EBUSY test, so a set na_kpriv with NAF_BUSY and no way for NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY to be false makes this branch rarely reachable); otherwise it allocates a private netmap_priv_d (ENOMEM on failure), sets its np_ifp, calls netmap_do_regif and, on failure, deletes the private data, restores the hardware adapter's memory with netmap_mem_restore and returns the error; on success it stores the private data in bna->na_kpriv, sets NAF_BUSY in na->na_flags and returns 0. For any other request type (detach): it returns EINVAL without changes if na->active_fds is 0; otherwise it deletes bna->na_kpriv, sets it to NULL, clears NAF_BUSY, restores the hardware adapter's memory and returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY makes the already-attached case return EBUSY first in practice (netmap_bdg.c:1678-1684, 1695-1696). Original reviewer right that detach with active_fds == 0 returns EINVAL with na_kpriv and NAF_BUSY untouched (1698-1699) and that the attach error path restores memory (1692). Real function at 1661-1707 (slice 1545-1795). Read in full; NETMAP_OWNED_BY_ANY's definition was not read.

name: netmap_mem_finalize
prose: Precondition: nmd is a valid allocator and na a valid adapter; the caller does not hold the allocator lock. If nm_mem_check_group(nmd, na->pdev) is negative it returns ENOMEM immediately without locking the allocator. Otherwise it takes NMA_LOCK and calls netmap_mem_config; if that returns nonzero it jumps to the exit without incrementing nmd->active and without calling nmd_finalize, and the value returned is whatever nmd->lasterr currently holds. If the config succeeds it increments nmd->active, calls ops->nmd_finalize(nmd, na) and stores its result in nmd->lasterr, and when that is zero and NETMAP_MEM_NOMAP is clear it maps the buffer pool with netmap_mem_map and stores that result in lasterr. At the exit it copies nmd->lasterr to a local, releases the lock, calls netmap_mem_deref(nmd, na) if that value is nonzero, and returns it.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the netmap_mem_config failure path (netmap_mem2.c:368-369) skips the increment and the nmd_finalize call, and the old prose omitted it; note the returned value on that path is the previous nmd->lasterr, so it can be 0 even though the config failed (what netmap_mem_config sets in lasterr was not read). Original reviewer right that the group-check ENOMEM return happens before any locking (362-364). Real function at 358-387 (slice 253-512). Read in full.

name: netmap_get_pipe_na
prose: Precondition: hdr is a netmap request whose nr_body is a register request, na is an output pointer, the caller holds NMG_LOCK. It looks for '{' (master) or '}' (slave) in the port name; if neither is present the name is not a pipe and it returns 0 without touching *na. It returns EINVAL if the pipe id after the bracket is empty or the bracket is at the start, or if the register mode is not NR_REG_ALL_NIC or NR_REG_ONE_NIC. It then looks up the parent port with netmap_get_na (on an ENXIO error it tries once to create a persistent VALE port with the NMG_LOCK temporarily released, otherwise it returns the error). If the parent is owned by the kernel it releases it with netmap_unget_na and returns EBUSY. If a pipe with that id already exists it picks the endpoint with the requested role (or its peer), releases the parent reference with netmap_unget_na and goes to found. If not found and create is 0 it releases the parent and returns ENODEV. Otherwise it allocates a master and a slave pipe adapter (ENOMEM on allocation failure), registers them with netmap_attach_common (an error frees what was built, removes the master from the parent with netmap_pipe_remove and releases the parent through netmap_unget_na) and netmap_pipe_add, links them as peers, takes references on the parent and on ifp (if non-NULL) and a peer reference on the opposite endpoint. At found it sets *na to the requested endpoint, takes a reference on it and returns 0.
note: The packet name netmap_pipe_alloc is not a function in netmap_pipe.c; the slice 766-863 is the second half of netmap_get_pipe_na at netmap_pipe.c:652-860 (read from 656 to 850 with comment lines skipped). It is fixed under that real name instead of being dropped. The old prose claimed netmap_unget_na on every exit path; in the code the successful create path keeps the parent and ifp references (823-826) and only the failure and found paths call it.

name: ntsync_wait_check_ready
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the owner's private lock (NTSYNC_PRIV_ASSERT) and state is a valid wait state. If state->ready is already true it returns without doing anything. For an 'all' wait it calls ntsync_wait_all_prepare: if that returns true (and, asserted with MPASS, stop is false) it calls ntsync_wait_all_commit, sets state->ready to true and calls ntsync_wait_post_commit; if it returns false with stop set, this function does nothing more (what the prepare step already changed in state, for example an index, was not read); if it returns false without stop and an alert event exists, it asks the alert object whether it is signaled at index obj_count - 1 and, if so, sets state->index to that index, consumes it, runs its post_commit and sets state->ready to true. For an 'any' wait it calls ntsync_wait_any(state) and sets state->ready to true if that returns true (the internals of that call, including whether it consumes the signaled object, were not read); if it returns false state->ready stays false. The function returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that on the stop path state->index may already have been set by the prepare step, so 'left unchanged' was not justified (ntsync.c:178-184); the prose now says only that this function changes nothing further. Original reviewer's claim about 'any' waits (no commit or post_commit here) matches the code at 195-197, where the work is inside ntsync_wait_any, which was not read. Real function at 164-199 (slice 1-251). Read in full.

name: nvmft_controller_lun_changed
prose: Precondition: ctrlr is a valid controller with an initialised lock and changed_ns list; the caller does not hold ctrlr->lock. It computes new_nsid = lun_id + 1 and takes ctrlr->lock. If the changed-namespace list is not already marked full (ns[0] != 0xffffffff) it scans the sorted list: if new_nsid is already present it releases the lock and returns without reporting anything. Otherwise, if the last list slot is non-zero (the list is full) it resets the list and sets ns[0] to the full marker 0xffffffff; else it inserts new_nsid at its sorted position (shifting later entries). Whether it inserted, reset the list, or found the list already marked full, it then checks changed_ns_reported: if it is already true it releases the lock and returns; otherwise it sets it to true, releases the lock and calls nvmft_report_aer for an NS attribute change event (log page NVME_LOG_CHANGED_NAMESPACE), which may itself drop the event depending on the AER mask and pending state. The lock is released on every path and no memory is allocated.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the AER is also reported when the list was already marked full (nvmft_controller.c:1106, 1139-1147), not only when an insertion happened. Original reviewer right that nvmft_report_aer may drop the event. A duplicate nsid returns before any report (1110-1113). Real function at 1093-1148 (slice 1053-1148). Read in full; nvmft_report_aer not read.

name: update_cc
prose: Precondition: ctrlr and ctrlr->np are valid and the caller does not hold ctrlr->lock. It sets *need_shutdown to false and takes the lock. It returns false (with the lock released and ctrlr->cc unchanged) if ctrlr->shutdown is already set or if _nvmf_validate_cc(np->max_io_qsize, np->cap, ctrlr->cc, new_cc) fails. Otherwise it records the changed bits, stores new_cc in ctrlr->cc, and: if the SHN field changed and new_cc has a nonzero SHN, it sets CSTS.SHST to the shutdown-occurring value, clears CC.EN in ctrlr->cc (so ctrlr->cc then differs from new_cc), sets ctrlr->shutdown and *need_shutdown to true and logs; if the EN bit changed, a new EN of 0 logs a reset request and sets ctrlr->shutdown and *need_shutdown to true, while a new EN of 1 sets CSTS.RDY. It releases the lock and returns true.
note: Both reviewers right: the old precondition ('not shutting down and validation passes') is replaced because the function returns false in those cases (nvmft_controller.c:815-823), and CC.EN is cleared after new_cc is stored on a shutdown request (826-833), so ctrlr->cc may not equal new_cc. Real function at 804-851 (slice 799-1052). Read in full; _nvmf_validate_cc not read here (see its own entry).

name: _nvmf_validate_cc
prose: Precondition: none; it only reads its arguments and has no side effects. It returns false if any of these hold for new_cc: its IOCQES field is nonzero and not 4; its IOSQES field is nonzero and not 6; with STRICT_CHECKS defined, either of those two fields is nonzero while max_io_qsize is 0 (max_io_qsize is otherwise unused); its SHN field is 3; its AMS field is nonzero; its MPS field is below the CAP MPSMAX field or above the CAP MPSMIN field (as coded, in this order of comparison); its CSS field is neither 0 nor 7; or the CC.EN bit is set in old_cc and the AMS, MPS or CSS field differs between old_cc and new_cc. Otherwise it returns true.
note: Round 15 reviewer's point (STRICT_CHECKS extra false cases) is already part of the prose as stated above (nvmft_subr.c:77-80, 90-93); the formal contract was empty. The MPS comparison is described as the code writes it (106-109); whether MPSMAX and MPSMIN are meant that way round was not examined. Function at 64-123 (slice 1-219). Read in full.

name: nvmf_receive_capsule
prose: Precondition: arg is the host qpair, nc a received completion capsule; the caller does not hold qp->lock. It sets sc->ka_active_rx_traffic to 1 if keep-alive traffic tracking is enabled. If the completion's CID is greater than qp->num_commands it logs, calls nvmf_disconnect, frees the capsule and returns before taking qp->lock and before updating the submission queue head. Otherwise it takes qp->lock and updates qp->sqhd (from the completion if flow control is on and the field is valid, else by incrementing it modulo num_commands + 1). If qp->qp is NULL (the queue pair is shut down) it logs, releases the lock, frees the capsule and returns without invoking any callback and without disconnecting. If no active command exists for the CID it releases the lock, logs, calls nvmf_disconnect, frees the capsule and returns. Otherwise it takes the command's request: if no requests are pending it clears the CID's active slot, returns the command to the free list and releases the lock; if requests are pending it binds the first pending request to the command and calls nvmf_dispatch_command (the lock is not released in this function on that branch; whether nvmf_dispatch_command releases it was not read). Finally it calls the completed request's callback with the CQE, frees the capsule and frees the request.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the invalid-CID path returns before qp->lock and before the SQ head update (nvmf_qpair.c:191-197), and the old text said lock taken and released on every path. Original reviewer right about the shutdown path (216-223). Real function at 170-252 (slice 1-253). Read in full; nvmf_dispatch_command not read.

name: ocs_add_new_tgt
prose: Precondition: node and fcp are valid and fcp->sim is a valid SIM; the target table fcp->tgt has OCS_MAX_TARGETS entries. It looks for the first slot i with state OCS_TGT_STATE_NONE; if there is none, i is left equal to OCS_MAX_TARGETS (the code does not check this and goes on to use i as the target id, and then calls ocs_update_tgt with that index, which would index past the table if it uses it as a table index; ocs_update_tgt was not read). It allocates a ccb with xpt_alloc_ccb_nowait; if that fails it prints a message and returns (uint32_t)-1 (the function returns uint32_t, so -1 becomes 0xFFFFFFFF). It creates a path for the SIM with target id i and the wildcard LUN; if that fails it prints a message, frees the ccb and returns (uint32_t)-1. Otherwise it calls ocs_update_tgt(node, fcp, i), queues a rescan of the path with xpt_rescan(ccb) and returns 0. On the two failure returns no target slot has been changed.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: the function is declared uint32_t (ocs_cam.c:1030) so the -1 returns are unsigned conversions, as the old prose said. Original reviewer right that with a full table the code uses i == OCS_MAX_TARGETS without a check (1037-1056). Real function at 1030-1059 (slice 1035-1291 started inside it). Read in full.

name: ocs_target_io
prose: Precondition: ocs and ccb are valid and ccb is a target SCSI I/O ccb whose csio.tag_id identifies an IO in the driver's IO table. It looks the IO up with ocs_scsi_find_io; if none is found it sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR and panics (the following return 1 is not reached). If the IO already has OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_RECV set it also sets OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_CAM and returns 1: with CAM_SEND_STATUS set it sets CAM_REQ_CMP and frees the IO with ocs_target_io_free; without it it sets CAM_REQ_ABORTED and leaves the IO allocated. Otherwise it records the ccb in the IO, sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_INPROG with CAM_SIM_QUEUED, and then: if CAM_SEND_STATUS is set and the transfer length is 0 it sets IO state RESP and calls ocs_scsi_send_resp (with sense data when CAM_SEND_SENSE is set); else if the transfer length is nonzero it sets state DATA, builds the SGL and, if the SGL has entries, calls ocs_scsi_send_rd_data for CAM_DIR_IN or ocs_scsi_recv_wr_data for CAM_DIR_OUT (any other direction sets CAM_REQ_INVALID and rc = 1), while an SGL build that gives no entries sets CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR and rc = 1; if neither condition holds (no status and no data) it sets CAM_REQ_INVALID and rc = 1. The completion callback registered with the hardware calls is ocs_scsi_target_io_cb. If rc is nonzero (including the value returned by the send/recv calls) it then sets the ccb status to CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR (overwriting a previous CAM_REQ_INVALID), clears CAM_SIM_QUEUED, sets the IO state to OCS_CAM_IO_DATA_DONE and, when CAM_SEND_STATUS was set with zero transfer length, frees the IO. It returns rc: 0 when the IO was handed to the hardware, otherwise 1 or the nonzero code from the hardware calls.
note: Round 15 reviewer is partly right and partly wrong: failure paths do first set CAM_REQ_INVALID, but it is then overwritten by CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR in the rc != 0 block (ocs_cam.c:1820-1823); and the zero-transfer sendstatus failure DOES free the IO (1826-1828), so that part of his claim is wrong. Original reviewer right that a bad tag panics and that a failing send call sets the ccb status in the rc block. Real function at 1718-1832 (slice 1547-1819). Read in full; the send and SGL helpers not read.

name: ocs_scsi_recv_tmf
prose: Precondition: tmfio and tmfio->node->sport are valid; abortio must be non-NULL when cmd is OCS_SCSI_TMF_ABORT_TASK (it is dereferenced there without a check). It returns 1 if the sport's tgt_data is NULL. It picks the target resource for the LUN (the enabled per-LUN entry if lun < OCS_MAX_LUN, else the enabled wildcard entry, else none) and takes the first immediate-notify ccb (INOT) queued on it. If there is no INOT it logs, completes abortio (if non-NULL) and tmfio with ocs_scsi_io_complete and returns -1. Otherwise it stores abortio in tmfio, removes the INOT from the queue, fills in tag, sequence id, initiator id and status CAM_MESSAGE_RECV and the LUN, and by cmd: ABORT_TASK sets the abort message and the abort-task tag and sets the OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_RECV and ABORT_NOTIFY flags on abortio; ABORT_TASK_SET, CLEAR_TASK_SET, QUERY_ASYNCHRONOUS_EVENT, LOGICAL_UNIT_RESET, CLEAR_ACA and TARGET_RESET set the corresponding message in the INOT; QUERY_TASK_SET logs that it is unsupported, puts the INOT back at the tail of the queue, completes tmfio and returns -1; any other cmd logs, puts the INOT back and returns -1 without completing tmfio. For the supported commands it sets rc to 0, prints a trace and passes the INOT to CAM with xpt_done, and if abortio is non-NULL it sets OCS_CAM_IO_F_ABORT_DEV on it and returns the result of ocs_scsi_tgt_abort_io(abortio, ocs_io_abort_cb, tmfio); otherwise it returns 0.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the default unsupported-command path requeues the INOT but does not complete tmfio (ocs_cam.c:774-778), unlike QUERY_TASK_SET (748-754). Original reviewer right that QUERY_TASK_SET returns -1 and that ABORT_TASK needs a non-NULL abortio. Real function at 681-799 (slice 507-780 cut the tail). Read in full; helper functions not read.

name: __ocs_domain_wait_alloc
prose: Precondition: ctx is a domain state-machine context in the wait-alloc state, evt a domain event, arg the per-event argument (passed only to __ocs_domain_common). The handler returns NULL on every path. For OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ALLOC_OK: it reads the optional wwn_bump property, takes domain->sport (ocs_assert returns NULL, logging, if it is NULL), copies the service parameters from the domain DMA buffer into domain->service_params and sport->service_params (and into flogi_service_params when femul_enable is set), writes the port and node names from sport->wwpn and sport->wwnn into the sport's service parameter block (XORing them with wwn_bump when it is nonzero), then: for a loop domain that is not an NL port it transitions to __ocs_domain_allocated and calls __ocs_domain_attach_internal(domain, sport->fc_id); otherwise it looks for the fabric controller node: if one exists it logs and breaks out of the case without any transition; else it allocates a fabric node (a failure is only logged) and, if allocated, pauses or transitions it to __ocs_fabric_init, then sets domain->req_accept_frames to 1 and transitions to __ocs_domain_allocated (also after an allocation failure). For OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ALLOC_FAIL it logs and sets domain->req_domain_free to 1. OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_FOUND does nothing. OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_LOST logs and transitions to __ocs_domain_wait_domain_lost. Any other event is passed to __ocs_domain_common.
note: Both reviewers right: the sport and domain service-parameter names are updated in the service parameter block, not in sport->wwpn itself (ocs_domain.c:672-681), and the fabric-node allocation failure does not stop the transition to __ocs_domain_allocated (706-720); the existing-fabric-node path breaks without transition (702-705) and DOMAIN_LOST transitions to wait_domain_lost (736-739). Real function at 638-747 (slice 506-764). Read in full.

name: __ocs_p2p_wait_domain_attach
prose: Precondition: ctx is the state-machine context of a transient point-to-point node. The handler returns NULL on every path. OCS_EVT_ENTER holds the node's frames (ocs_node_hold_frames) and OCS_EVT_EXIT accepts them again (ocs_node_accept_frames). OCS_EVT_DOMAIN_ATTACH_OK first asserts that sport->p2p_winner is set (ocs_assert returns NULL, logging, if not), then looks for a node with fc_id sport->p2p_remote_port_id: if one exists it is left untouched (asserted to be a different node than this one); otherwise it allocates a new remote node (on failure it logs and returns NULL immediately, leaving the transient node neither reinitialised nor shut down), calls ocs_fabric_notify_topology(node) and transitions the new node to __ocs_p2p_rnode_init. After that, if this node's rnode.fc_id is 0 it reinitialises the node for device login with ocs_node_init_device(node, FALSE), otherwise it sets the shutdown reason to OCS_NODE_SHUTDOWN_DEFAULT and calls ocs_fabric_initiate_shutdown(node). Any other event is passed, with arg, to __ocs_fabric_common.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: arg is not unused, it is passed to __ocs_fabric_common in the default case (ocs_fabric.c:1392-1394). Original reviewer right that an allocation failure returns NULL before the transient node is reinitialised or shut down (1366-1370). Real function at 1333-1398 (slice 1290-1542). Read in full; callees not read.

name: ocs_hw_set_persistent_topology
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised ocs_hw_t with a ready SLI context; topology is OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_AUTO, OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_NPORT or OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_LOOP; opts is OCS_CMD_POLL or anything else (treated as the no-wait, semaphore-waiting mode). It builds a set-features parameter: AUTO becomes P2P-with-failover on a Lancer ASIC and P2P-only otherwise, NPORT becomes P2P-only, LOOP becomes FC-AL-only; any other topology logs and returns -1 before any command is built. It initialises a semaphore, builds the SET_FEATURES persistent-topology mailbox command and, for OCS_CMD_POLL, submits it with ocs_hw_command in polling mode, returning that function's nonzero result (after logging) if it fails. In the other mode it submits it with OCS_CMD_NOWAIT and the callback ocs_hw_set_persistent_topolgy_cb (which stores the completion status and posts the semaphore), returns the nonzero ocs_hw_command result if submission fails, waits on the semaphore forever (returning -ENXIO if the wait fails) and returns -EFAULT if the callback stored a nonzero status. When no error occurred it records the topology in the SLI context with sli_config_persistent_topology and returns the (zero) result code. No locks are taken here.
note: The packet name ocs_hw_set_persistent_topolgy (with the typo) matches only the callback ocs_hw_set_persistent_topolgy_cb at ocs_hw.c:12136-12146; the function the prose describes is ocs_hw_set_persistent_topology at 12178-12250 (read in full), so it is fixed under that name. Reviewer reasons were only mechanical. Return type is ocs_hw_rtn_e, so the negative values are as coded at 12212, 12238 and 12243.

name: ocs_hw_io_abort
prose: Precondition: hw and io_to_abort are valid, hw->state is OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE and io_to_abort has a live reference. It returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR for NULL arguments or a state other than OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE, and OCS_HW_RTN_IO_NOT_ACTIVE if ocs_ref_get_unless_zero on the IO's reference fails (nothing taken). After taking a reference it returns OCS_HW_RTN_IO_NOT_ACTIVE (dropping the reference) if the IO has no work queue, and OCS_HW_RTN_IO_ABORT_IN_PROGRESS (dropping its own reference but leaving the flag that another abort set) if abort_in_progress is already set. Otherwise, under io_abort_lock, it sets abort_in_progress, stores the callback and argument, and allocates a request tag with ocs_hw_reqtag_alloc; if that fails it returns OCS_HW_RTN_NO_RESOURCES without dropping the reference and without clearing abort_in_progress. With a tag, if the IO's WQE is still on the work queue's list it marks the WQE as needing an abort submission (storing send_abts, id and abort tag) and returns 0 with the reference and abort_in_progress retained. Otherwise it builds the ABORT WQE with sli_abort_wqe (failure sets rc to OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR and frees the tag), selects a work queue if the IO had none and writes the WQE with hw_wq_write (a positive result is treated as 0). If the final rc is not OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS it clears abort_in_progress under the lock and drops the reference; it returns rc (0 after a successful submission, in which case the reference is held until the abort completes).
note: Round 15 reviewer is right that the IO_ABORT_IN_PROGRESS path drops the reference but must not clear abort_in_progress, which belongs to the other abort (ocs_hw.c:4918-4925). Original reviewer is right about the request-tag allocation failure (4955-4959, leaves the reference and flag set) but wrong about ABORT WQE failure, which does clear the flag and drop the reference via the final block (5004-5009). Real function at 4877-5011 (slice 4729-4986). Read in full; the callee functions not read.

name: ocs_hw_get
prose: Precondition: hw is an initialised ocs_hw_t and value is NULL or a writable uint32_t. If value is NULL it returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR without dereferencing it (hw is not checked for NULL in the part read). Otherwise it sets *value to 0 and switches on prop, returning OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS with *value set from the matching configuration, SLI or link field for each recognised property, except: OCS_HW_AUTO_XFER_RDY_BLK_SIZE returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR (with *value 0) for an unrecognised block-size code; OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY returns OCS_HW_TOPOLOGY_NONE with success when hw->link.speed is 0 whatever the topology field holds, and otherwise maps the link topology to NPORT, LOOP or NONE, returning OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR with *value left 0 for any other topology value; OCS_HW_LINK_CONFIG_SPEED maps the configured speed to 0 (auto), 2000, 4000, 8000, 10000, 16000 or 32000 and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR (value 0) for any other configured speed; OCS_HW_RESET_REQUIRED calls sli_reset_required and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR if that is negative; any unrecognised prop logs and returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR with *value 0. It takes no locks.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: with link.speed == 0 the topology case returns NONE and success before looking at the topology (ocs_hw.c:1565-1572), so the 'unrecognised topology gives error' claim only holds when the link speed is nonzero. Real function at 1481-1767 (slice 1569-1843 started inside it). Partly read: lines 1481-1627 were read in full; for lines 1628-1767 only the case labels and the return and rc lines were read (the handling of OCS_HW_SGL_CHAINING_ALLOWED, SEND_FRAME_CAPABLE and the other simple property cases there was not examined line by line).

name: ocs_hw_init
prose: Precondition: hw is an ocs_hw_t that has been set up (ocs_hw_setup) or reset. Under cmd_lock it returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR immediately if the cmd_head or cmd_pending lists are not empty. It frees the receive buffers with ocs_hw_rx_free and rebuilds the IO free lists. The remaining steps each return on failure: a sequence of sub-steps (auto xfer ready configuration, SLI init, health check, queue initialisation and count checks against the SLI maxima, header template registration, rnode memory allocation, RQ buffer and sequence pool allocation, rpi_ref set-up, FCFI/MRQ registration, reqtag and IO set-up) returns either OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR, OCS_HW_RTN_NO_MEMORY (for the allocation failures at the lines near 755, 795 and 809) or the failing sub-step's rc; earlier-allocated resources are not released on those returns, except that rnode_mem is freed on one failure path and payload_memory on another. After that it initialises queue history, queries the link configuration, sets the Ethernet license if applicable (failure only logged), and on a Lancer-type interface calls ocs_hw_set_dif_seed: a failure returns the current rc (which can still be OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS) at once, before any queue is armed or the state is made active; on a BE3-type interface with DIF capability ocs_hw_set_dif_mode is called and a failure returns its rc. It then arms every event queue and every completion queue (sli_queue_arm), adds receive, work and completion queues to the lookup hashes (the receive and work queues are not armed here), sets hw->state to OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE, initialises the rqpair (failure only logged), starts the WQE timer if configured, allocates the send-frame IOs (failures logged), configures the watchdog if requested (failures logged), allocates domain_dmem and fcf_dmem (OCS_HW_RTN_NO_MEMORY if either fails) and loop_map (a failure there is only logged), and returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: only the event queues and completion queues are armed (ocs_hw.c:945-947, 966-969). Round 17 reviewer is right: a failed ocs_hw_set_dif_seed returns rc, which may be success, before arming and before the state becomes ACTIVE (926-930). Real function at 533-1033 (slice 763-1016). Partly read: lines 905-1033 were read in full; for 533-905 only the lock check, the list handling and the return lines were read, so the individual sub-steps listed above are described by their return statements and not checked line by line.

name: ocs_hw_wq_process_io
prose: Precondition: arg is a valid ocs_hw_io_t with a valid hw pointer, cqe is the work-queue completion entry for it and status its completion status; for an OCS_HW_IO_TARGET_RSP IO that is port-owned, io->axr_buf is valid and the caller does not hold io->axr_lock. The function returns nothing. It handles quarantine: if the IO is in its first quarantine phase it sets io->quarantine from the CQE and re-queues it with ocs_hw_io_quarantine, clears quarantine_first_phase, and does the same for a secondary IO that is still quarantined. It removes the IO's timed WQE, clears io->xbusy if the CQE's XB bit is 0, and derives len (and ext for ELS requests) from the CQE according to io->type; for a port-owned target response it takes io->axr_lock (recording that) and notes whether the out-of-order AXR command and data callbacks are flagged. If status is nonzero it reads the extended status and may call ocs_hw_io_abort: for an originator IO with config.i_only_aab when an abort is needed (abort with send_abts TRUE), or for a non-originator IO whose XB bit is set (send_abts FALSE); if the abort returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS it saves status, ext and len in io->saved_* with status_saved set and jumps to the exit, skipping everything below (no sec_hio free, no done callback, no AXR callbacks); any other result, including OCS_HW_RTN_IO_ABORT_IN_PROGRESS, is only logged and processing continues. Next it frees io->sec_hio if present and clears it; if io->done is non-NULL it clears io->done, replaces status, len and ext with the saved values if status_saved was set (clearing it), restores the SGL and calls done once. Then, only if the out-of-order AXR command flag was set, it delivers the command sequence to the bounce callback (when config.bounce is set and a bounce callback exists) or to the unsolicited callback, and, only inside that same block, if the AXR data flag was also set, delivers the data sequence the same way. At the exit label it releases io->axr_lock if it was taken.
note: Round 15 and 17 reviewers are right: the AXR data sequence is delivered only inside the out_of_order_axr_cmd block (ocs_hw.c:8798-8826), and a successful abort jumps to the exit before it. Real function at 8580-8832 (slice 8596-8851 cut the head). Read in full; the called helper functions not read.

name: ocs_hw_cb_fip
prose: Precondition: ctx is a valid ocs_hw_t and e a valid sli4_fip_event_t (both ocs_hw_assert-ed). Before the switch, for every event type, it looks up a domain: for SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_CLEAR_VLINK it scans the sport list of each non-NULL domain in hw->domains for a sport whose indicator equals event->index; for all other types it uses ocs_hw_domain_get_indexed(hw, event->index). Then by type: SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_DISCOVERED calls ocs_hw_read_fcf(hw, event->index) (the domain found is not used); SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_DEAD calls hw->callback.domain with OCS_HW_DOMAIN_LOST and the domain if both the domain and the callback are non-NULL; SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_CLEAR_VLINK does the same after setting domain->req_rediscover_fcf to TRUE; SLI4_FCOE_FIP_FCF_MODIFIED makes the same callback (when domain and callback are non-NULL) and then always calls ocs_hw_read_fcf(hw, event->index); any other type is only logged. The function returns 0 on every path and takes no locks.
note: Round 15 reviewer is wrong: FCF_MODIFIED does issue ocs_hw_read_fcf (ocs_hw.c:9367-9374). Original reviewer right that FCF_DISCOVERED reads the FCF regardless of the domain and that CLEAR_VLINK also sets req_rediscover_fcf (9348, 9363). The old text said the domain lookup was done for the lost-type events only; it is done for every type (9318-9344). Real function at 9307-9380 (slice 9106-9372 cut the tail). Read in full; ocs_hw_read_fcf not read.

name: ocs_xport_control
prose: Precondition: xport is a valid transport with xport->ocs non-NULL (both are ocs_assert-ed and return -1 if not); cmd is an OCS_XPORT_* command and the variable arguments match the command. OCS_XPORT_PORT_ONLINE calls ocs_hw_port_control(OCS_HW_PORT_INIT) and sets xport->configured_link_state to cmd on success; its result is the returned code (nonzero on failure). OCS_XPORT_PORT_OFFLINE calls the port shutdown control and sets configured_link_state on success; a failure is only logged and the function returns 0. OCS_XPORT_SHUTDOWN reads OCS_HW_RESET_REQUIRED (treated as 0 if the query fails); if a reset is required it calls ocs_xport_force_free and leaves the case at once, without registering the domain-list callback, without calling ocs_vport_del_all and with rc still 0. Otherwise it registers the domain-list-empty callback, issues the port shutdown (a failure calls ocs_xport_force_free), else waits on the semaphore for OCS_FC_DOMAIN_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_USEC (a timeout makes rc the nonzero wait result and calls ocs_xport_force_free); it then unregisters the callback and calls ocs_vport_del_all. OCS_XPORT_POST_NODE_EVENT returns -1 if the node or node->ocs is NULL (asserted) or the node state machine has no current state, otherwise posts the event with ocs_hw_async_call and waits for its semaphore forever: -1 if the async call or the wait fails, else 0. OCS_XPORT_WWNN_SET and WWPN_SET store the 64-bit value in xport->req_wwnn or req_wwpn and return 0. An unrecognised cmd returns 0. rc is a uint32_t returned through an int32_t.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: on the reset-required path SHUTDOWN force-frees and breaks before ocs_vport_del_all (ocs_xport.c:793-797). Real function at 750-917 (slice 757-1029). Read in full except logging lines; the hardware control and force-free functions were not read.

name: otus_set_key_cb
prose: Precondition: arg points to an otus_cmd_key. The function is inside an #ifdef notyet block in if_otus.c (lines 2948-3046), so it is not compiled in a normal build; in that block its non-group branch refers to a variable ni that is not declared in the function. It clears a ar_cmd_ekey; for a group key it uses the key id as uid and our own address with bit 0x80 set in the first byte as MAC, otherwise it uses OTUS_UID(associd) and ni->ni_macaddr. It sets kix to 0, maps the key cipher (WEP40, WEP104, TKIP, CCMP) to the hardware cipher and returns without sending anything for any other cipher. It copies up to 16 bytes of the key and sends AR_CMD_EKEY with otus_cmd; if that returns an error, or the cipher is not TKIP, it returns. For TKIP it then sets kix to 1, copies the next 16 key bytes (the MIC key) and sends a second AR_CMD_EKEY, ignoring its result. It returns nothing.
note: Round 15 reviewer is right: the first otus_cmd error is checked and causes an early return (if_otus.c:3006-3008); only the second command's result is ignored. Original reviewer right that an unsupported cipher is silently ignored and that the non-group path uses an undeclared ni (2984). Function at 2968-3014 (slice 2827-3080), inside notyet. Read in full.

name: p2sb_get_port
prose: Precondition: dev is unused. It compares unit with the number of entries in the static table lbg_communities (6 entries) and returns EINVAL if unit is not below that count (a negative unit is converted to a large unsigned value in the comparison and also returns EINVAL); otherwise it returns lbg_communities[unit], which is 0xAF, 0xAE, 0xAD, 0xAC, 0xAB or 0x11 for units 0 to 5. It has no side effects.
note: Read in full at p2sb.c:73-80 with the table at 59-61. Contract left empty because the result depends on a static table and an errno value.

name: PCCARD_ACCESSOR(vendor, VENDOR, uint32_t)
prose: Generated function pccard_get_vendor: a static inline int function taking (device_t dev, uint32_t *t), defined by that macro invocation in pccardvar.h, whose body is the single statement return BUS_READ_IVAR(device_get_parent(dev), dev, PCCARD_IVAR_VENDOR, (uintptr_t *)t). It returns whatever the parent bus read-ivar method returns for that ivar; on success that method stores the vendor id through the cast pointer, which is a pointer to uintptr_t aimed at an object of type uint32_t, so the width written is that of uintptr_t. The function itself makes no checks and takes no locks.
note: Name given as the macro invocation (pccardvar.h:207-213 definition; invocation in the 215-225 block) because the function is macro-generated. What the parent writes to *t on a nonzero return, and whether the stored value is borrowed or owned, was not read; the old prose claims about that were removed.
